1.1.text:
"It was Mayor Honey with a Harvest Festival brochure in the hidden grove!"

He took the credit, but none of the blame. "Well, what was I supposed to do? Just let him warn people against coming to our town? That's absolutely ridiculous! The Harvest Festival is the cornerstone of our economy!" Logico thought maybe it was more important to protect the lives of its citizens than its economy, but Irratino argued it was simply civic pride. Either way, the festival went ahead as planned, which delighted everyone, except, perhaps, the dead naysayer.

1.2.text:
"It was Corny Cordovan with pumpkin vines in the ticket booth!"

"Oh, so when the Harvest Festival advertisements said that people were dying to get in and try to win that prize skull, that was okay, but when the customers actually do kill to get in, suddenly that's wrong. Whatever happened to truth in advertising?!"

1.3.text:
"It was Just an Ordinary Scarecrow with my grandfather's axe in the corn maze!"

"But how is that possible?!" Logico said. "Ordinary scarecrows don’t ordinarily kill people. There must be a logical explanation!" "That's because it's not an ordinary scarecrow," said Leaf Collector Brown. "It was some kind of evil spirit! Some kind of living scarecrow, a demon creature of hate and straw who has a pumpkin for a head!" "You were right, Logico!" Irratino exclaimed. "There was a logical explanation!"

1.4.text:
"It was the Pumpkin Man with a corn on the cob at the food truck!"

Immediately, word spread throughout the entire festival. And despite the mayor's insistence that there was absolutely nothing to worry about, people began to whisper. And they began to do a lot more than whisper when they learned the identity of the victim... The leading contender for Harvest Monarch!

1.5.text:
"It was Auditor Gold with a pitchfork in the corn itself!"

"I thought it was the Pumpkin Man!" Auditor Gold exclaimed. "If I didn't kill him first, then he would've killed me second!" "Oh, that's a convenient excuse," replied Logico, "but we can all tell that you're really ... Mrs. Ruby, the [word obscured in scan] thief!" "How did you know?!" Auditor Gold exclaimed as she whipped off her headset, revealing herself none other to be the famous Mrs. Ruby. "You can replace your hat," Logico said, "and you can change your name, but you can't change your height, handedness, eye color, or hair color!" "We'll see about that, Logico!" she exclaimed. "You may have caught me today, but you'll never get back the Seven Skulls!" And with that, Mrs. Ruby disappeared into the crowd.

(Will you be able to spot her next time?)
1.5.transcriptionNote: One word is covered by a finger in the supplied scan and is marked in brackets.

1.6.text:
"It was Corny the Cob with a stale churro in the long line!"

But when Deductive Logico said that, Corny the Cob took off. And though Irratino and Logico chased after the costumed villain, he outwitted them. He ran around the administration trailer. When they rounded the corner, he was gone. But just when they had given up hope, Organizer Applebaum knocked open the doors of the administration trailer and pointed at the corn maze. "He ran into the maze!" he shouted. Logico and Irratino didn't waste any time: they ran in after him.

1.7.text:
"It was Streamer Infrared with a scythe by the scarecrow!"

"Okay, fine! I did it! I'm not the Pumpkin Man! I was just furious at this guy for ruining my shot. I was hoping to stream myself catching that horrible killer. That would get so many views!" "But now you are a killer!" Logico said. "Hey, that gets views, too!" The Harvest Festival had asked Streamer Infrared to leave, but once Organizer Applebaum heard how many views he was getting, he asked him to stay.

1.8.text:
"It was Organizer Applebaum with the Skull of Eseth in the administration trailer! Why? To keep anybody from winning!"

"You couldn't just cancel the contest. But once you heard the Skull of Eseth was priceless, you didn't want to give it away! So, you killed the leading contender for Harvest Monarch. (See Case 1.4: Food Courting Death) Then, you committed a murder dressed as Corny the Cob, before running around the administration trailer, taking off your costume, and telling us he ran into the corn maze. (See Case 1.6: The Wheel of Life and Death.)" "Aha! And it was perfectly organized!" he muttered. "I would have been able to keep the skull if it wasn't for you. But since you solved the case, rode all the rides, and ate so much corn, I guess I'll have to present you, Logico, as the winner of this year's Harvest King!"

Logico was momentarily so thrilled to have won that he almost forgot that Organizer Applebaum was responsible for so many murders. After considering that, it felt like a bit of bittersweet victory. "That's one down, six to go," Irratino remarked. "Hopefully they're not all this involved," Logico replied. "Oh, you didn't have a great time? Mythological creatures, costumed culprits, town secrets, and conspiracies? This was an ideal investigation, as far as I'm concerned." Logico was going to mention that seven people had died, but he didn't want to upset Irratino's mood. The two of them had successfully recovered a skull, and that was worth celebrating. When they told Curator Coppertone, he promised them a bonus for finding it!

If you figured out who was the Pumpkin King before this mystery, then give yourself an extra $250.

2.1.text:
"It was Father Mango with the lightning in the chapel!"

That was Irratino, who accused Father Mango of exploiting his close connections with the higher powers in order to strike down his enemy. "There's just been a lot of storms lately!" Father Mango protested. Logico found himself siding with the killer. After all, how could he really be responsible for a lightning bolt? But Irratino then found a lightning rod planted on the dead body, and it had the father's fingerprints all over it. That wasn't a good look for him, either.

2.2.text:
"It was Superfan Smoky with Ten Rich Bozos in her great big house!"

"I did it, but I had a good reason!" Superfan Smoky declared. "I wanted her to autograph my copy of her book, but just as I was about to meet with her in her attic, this crazy shadow monster attacked me! I had to defend myself! But then, once I killed them, I learned that the shadow monster had transformed back into a lawyer!" Irratino replied, "Hmm... it sounds like this is one of those places where the veil is thin between this world... and the world of the damned." But Logico thought it was more likely that Smoky was just lying.

2.3.text:
"It was Barrister Bluish with the Skull of Nasem in the basement!"

Of course, he didn't immediately confess: he immediately invoked his legal rights and began to prepare his defense, which he signaled was going to be based on his belief that he was being attacked by ghosts. But that would develop in the days to come. "We have the skull," Logico said. "Why should we stick around this spooky house when our job is done?" "We're on the precipice of discovering proof of the existence of ghosts. and you think we should leave! No, we have to stay and investigate!" Logico didn't think this was wise. On the one hand, he didn't believe in ghosts, so he didn't think they were likely to find any proof of their existence. On the other hand, the mansion was very spooky and it gave him the chills.

So both hands were in agreement! But before he could make this argument, Irratino went into the library to continue his investigation.

2.4.text:
"It was Crime Queen Caramel with The Thought of the Lily by the bookshelves!"

"Yes, I did it! But I'm not going to fill your head with some kind of nonsense about ghosts. I did it on purpose, because they wouldn't stop talking while I was trying to read." Everybody else nodded along with this, and there was even some murmuring that Crime Queen Caramel's panache might make her a worthy rival to Dame Obsidian, at least in the murdering-with-style department. The important thing for Logico, however, was that he had figured out the anagram for the author of Mystery in Murdle Earth. If you rearranged the letters of Nestor Nirti Picaro it spelled ... Inspector Irratino!

2.5.text:
"It was the Hunky Barbarian with the sword of power by the new ruins!"

And Logico had to admit he had been swept away by the storyline, and had spent the last several hours of this investigation invested in the story. But then, on the last page, he found a note written in Dame Obsidian's handwriting in the margins: Even though this novel is bad, it has inspired me to take matters into my own hands. Like the Hunky Barbarian I will go down into my basement and battle the ghosts that have haunted my house. "I know where Dame Obsidian is!" Logico said. "But we might have to hurry! Also, Irratino! I loved your book!"

2.6.text:
"It was Janitor Salmon with an exposed wire in the hole!"

"He was dead when I found him!" exclaimed Janitor Salmon. "I was trying to shock him back to life! I came in and he was like this, and there were ghosts!" Logico could never believe the things that people would say to get out of the guilt of committing a crime, but he had to admit that he felt a presence in the air. And he began to hear ringing bells, and to get sleepier and sleepier.

2.7.text:
"It was the Demon King with a flaming sword in the planes of Hell!"

And just as Logico had pronounced that verdict, he collapsed to the ground. And the world got dark and quiet, and he was completely alone except for his thoughts about the case.

2.8.text:
"It was Dame Obsidian to blame due to carbon monoxide in the basement. Why? Just bad safety practices!"

"Yes, Logico," Irratino replied. He was carrying Logico out of the mansion. He could hear ambulance sirens getting closer. "The whole house was filled with carbon monoxide from the old boiler downstairs." Suddenly, so many things made sense to Logico: In the book of poisons, the symptoms for carbon monoxide were clearly listed to include hallucinations (see Case 2.4: Death in the Dame's Library). The carbon monoxide detector didn't have any batteries in it (see Case 2.2: Murder in the Obsidian Mansion), so nobody would know. The inside plants had died, a lesser-known side effect of carbon monoxide poisoning, and the vibes in the house were all sleepy, except for the balcony, which was refreshing ...

because of the fresh air (see Case 2.3: The Crime of Butlercide). Clearly, the furnace in the basement was belching smoke, and endangering everyone in the house. "Hallucinations, madness ..." Logico said. "Yes, and most importantly, people losing consciousness! Which is what happened to you. You started ranting and raving about some kind of demon. But fortunately, I managed to hold my breath and get you out of there before I succumbed to the same fate. Dame Obsidian has been evacuated, too, and she's asked if we got her notes!" "Thanks, Irratino ..." Logico managed to say. "Did you get the skull?" "Of course I got the skull!" Irratino replied. "You kept calling it a Demon King! That's when I knew that something was wrong.

I think you've been spending a little too much time reading my novels, Logico!" If you figured out what was wrong with Obsidian Manor before this puzzle, then give yourself an extra $250.

3.1.text:
"It was Fisherman Flamingo with an attack goose on the cruise ship!"

"Well, of course I did it!" Fisherman Flamingo replied. "But only because the security guard said they wouldn't let me fish. That's not a crime, is it?" "Fishing's not a crime," Logico said. "But murder is." "Ooh, that's such a good closing line," Irratino added, ruining it. And unfortunately, their cruise was ruined today. The cruise ship was quarantined as a crime scene, and now they had no way to get to Amaranth Island.

3.2.text:
"It was Silverton the Legend with an exploding seagull in the crew cabin!"

"Oh, and so if a person says that I'm too old to play Logico in the TV show adaptation of Murdle, I'm just supposed to sit back and take it? Or am I not allowed to express my vitality through the time-honored tradition of homicide?" "No!" Logico said. "You are absolutely not!" And just to make sure everybody stayed safe, Captain Marigold went around and confiscated everybody's weapons.

3.3.text:
"It was Baron Maroon with a single sapphire on Amaranth Island!"

"This is great news!" Irratino exclaimed. "This gemstone means we're on the right track!" But then, seeing the mood of his fellow passengers, he added, "But it's still bad that someone had to get murdered with it." Mercifully, this awkward moment was interrupted by a loud groan on the ship. Captain Marigold went running by. "What was that sound?" Logico called to her. His question stopped her cold. She looked him straight in the eyes, or perhaps it would be better to say that she looked straight through his eyes. She had a thousand-yard stare, and then some, and she said, "Logico... there is a legend I need to tell you."

3.4.text:
"It was the Creature from the Deep Blue Sea with giant teeth on the ghost ship!"

The captain spoke every word in her deep, salty voice, and when the story was done, Logico gave Irratino a look that said I don't believe this happened, only to find Irratino wearing a look that said I can't believe this happened, which actually meant the exact opposite. But before they had a chance to ask any follow-up questions, the ship arrived at their destination: Amaranth Island.

3.5.text:
"It was Baron Maroon with the Skull of Rewe in the lighthouse!"

"But Logico wasn't finished: "But, in fact, it's not Baron Maroon at all, but Mrs. Ruby in disguise!" "Fine!" Mrs. Ruby said, placing her distinctive hat upon her head. "I admit it! I did it!" "We'll be confiscating this for evidence!" Irratino said, taking advantage of the situation. The two of them packed up and took their small boat back to their big boat, which was anchored offshore. What they found there horrified them .. (Did you spot Mrs. Ruby? If so, give yourself $50).

3.6.text:
"It was nobody with something jagged in the bowels of the ship!"

"No," said Captain Marigold. "It wasn't nobody that killed these sailors. It was the Creature from the Deep Blue Sea. We've got ourselves a sea monster aboard, and there's nothing we can do about it but look for him, find him, and kill him ourselves." Logico didn't believe in sea monsters, and Irratino didn't believe they should be killed. But it certainly seemed to fit the evidence...

3.7.text:
"It was the Creature from the Deep Blue Sea with seawater sludge by a pile of metal!"

That was Irratino. Logico didn't love him jumping to conclusions. After all, they hadn't really seen the Creature from the Deep Blue Sea. "But Logico," Irratino said, "we're not jumping to conclusions. We're simply following the results of our logical deductions." "But we don't know there's even a Creature from the Deep Blue Sea!" "Then who are the legends about? And who killed these people and got rid of their bodies?" Irratino asked with the tone of someone who knew he was right even if he wasn't. But they didn't have the opportunity to debate what to do any further because Sailor Aero suddenly screamed, "Abandon ship, everyone! We're going down!"

3.8.text:
"It was Captain Marigold with the Skull of Rewe beside the big rock. Why? To cover up a huge mistake!"

"There never was a Creature from the Deep Blue Sea!" Logico shouted. "You hit an iceberg as we were approaching Amaranth Island—what we thought was a loud groaning noise was actually the hull being ripped apart (see Case 3.3: Look Out for Murder!). There was a big pile of metal in the bowels of the ship: that was the hastily constructed patch over the hole (see Case 3.7: Death in the Bowels). And when Silverton the Legend killed a safety officer, that eliminated the last chance someone had of saving our ship (see Case 3.2: Feathers & Rust: A Cargo Ship Killing). "Why did it look like that poor passenger was killed by nobody?

Not because nobody was actually the Creature from the Deep Blue Sea, but because they were injured when the metal hull was ripped up by the iceberg (see Case 3.6: How Can You Be Bored When There's a Murder on Board?). Captain Marigold was trying to cover up her incompetence with wild legends of sea creatures, and it almost worked! But you can only lie for so long until the boat sinks." "Well, great job, Logico," Captain Marigold said. "Unfortunately, we're still marooned on this tiny island, aren't we?" "Ha!" Irratino said. "You think Logico doesn't have a plan to get us off this island? He has a plan for everything, and—okay, I can tell from his face that he doesn't."

If you guessed what the Creature from the Deep Dark Blue really was, then give yourself an extra $250.

4.1.text:
"Major Red is with the People's Army in the Madding Mountains!"

Deductive Logico and Inspector Irratino made their way to the Madding Mountains, and they met up with Major Red. "Welcome, Logico! My old friend!" Logico was surprised by this, because the last time they had seen each other, Major Red had tried to kill them. But Logico didn't want to remind him of that. He wanted to think of a very subtle way to bring up the question that had brought the two detectives to him. "Where's the Skull of Dennivet?" Irratino blurted out immediately. "Ha!" Major Red replied. "Straight to the point! Come with me, and I will tell you."

4.2.text:
"It was Sergeant Lime with a piano on the balcony!"

"Sure! I did it! But it was because he didn't believe in the Skull of Dennivet! If somebody doesn't believe that it makes you invulnerable, well, we've gotta do something about it! That kind of disbelief has to result in consequences!" Irratino agreed with this in principle, but not in execution. Logico thought that belief shouldn't have to be enforced at the point of a bayonet, or, in this case, by the bottom of a piano. They both wanted to know more about the Skull of Dennivet, though. Like, where he got it. And where he was keeping it now. "I'll tell you how I got it," Major Red replied, answering their second most important question...

4.3.text:
"It was the Ghostly Dowager with the Skull of Dennivet in the tower!"

Major Red smiled when he had told the story. "And so, I am sure you see what it means: with the Skull of Dennivet, even death could not stop my army. And so, I traveled through the Screaming Forest and up the Madding Mountains to the abandoned Castle Eminence. There, I found the Skull of Dennivet, just as it had been in my dream. As soon as I got it, I felt its power pulsing through me. And I knew then that I was invincible." "That's a great story," Irratino said. "Very reasonable." Logico had a few questions, but before he could ask them, Major Red had to leave. "War never sleeps, gentlemen!"

4.4.text:
"It was Private Perriwinkle with a tracking device in No Man’s Land!"

"Sure, I killed him!" Private Perriwinkle declared. "He was going to have us rush the trenches! But if we did that, we were all going to die. So, the way I see it, I actually saved lives!" Logico thought that had a certain logic to it. Irratino agreed. Major Red, however, did not. "If you had charged, the Skull of Dennivet would have protected you! Now ..." Well, he took Private Perriwinkle into another room. Logico and Irratino didn’t ask many questions, because they were surrounded by armed guards. But they could make assumptions!

4.5.text:
"It was Tiny Taupe with the Skull of Dennivet in the Red Bay!"

"General amnesty!" Major Red called out. Although it was very clear that the amnesty applied only to his soldiers, and generally only for the crimes he approved of them committing. But they had won the war (at least for now), and so they got to make the rules. "So, Logico, I guess the Skull of Dennivet really was real?" Logico didn't know what to say about that: it was true that Major Red had rallied his troops, scattered and lost in the woods, and marched into St. Lupine where they had taken over the city he once called home. But also... "Wait a second, Irratino," Logico said. "What is this?" Logico picked up the Skull of Dennivet and realized... "It's broken in two." "What?" "It's cracked."

And then he pulled the Skull of Dennivet apart with his hands. "It's made of plaster, Irratino! This isn't the real skull at all! Major Red lied to us!" "Well, he is known for that," Irratino replied, "but then, where is the skull?" But the moment he said it, a smile spread across his face. "No," Logico said, "No. I don't believe it. No. I refuse."

4.6.text:
"It was Feral Child Olivine with a rock in the mysterious cave!"

Olivine hissed, chirped, and pecked at the two of them, and while Logico was confused, Irratino understood completely. "She says that he was an intruder into her cave, so she killed him, and that if we don't keep moving she'll kill us, too." Deductive Logico didn't agree with this morally, but he did agree with it practically. Better to continue on with their mission than be killed in a cave, most would agree.

4.7.text:
"It was Creepy Caretaker Carmine with the Skull of Dennivet in the dungeon!"

"But he was an interloper! He was going to damage the great Castle Eminence, which I have been entrusted to care for!" Logico and Irratino looked around. This place was in ruins. If he had been entrusted to care for it, then he was doing a pretty terrible job. But instead of arguing the point, Irratino took the initiative of confiscating the Skull of Dennivet. "We'll be taking this," he said, and then he turned to Logico and added, "See ... it was here. Just as I suspected, Major Red did have a prophetic dream. But, of course, he was not enough of a believer to follow his heart."

Logico thought that the problem with Major Red was certainly not that he didn't believe in himself, but before he could make the point, Creepy Caretaker Carmine returned to the two of them with an old sword, which he began swinging at them. This time, they agreed on the right course of action: they fled.

4.8.text:
"It was Major Red with the Skull of Dennivet in the bone pile. Why? To get the skull!"

"Haha, fools! I made up the whole concept of the skull in order to rally my troops. When you exposed it as a fake, I needed a skull bad. I knew you'd lead me right to it. And you did! Now, I'll be able to keep the loyalty of my people for many wars to come!" But wait—Inspector Irratino didn't understand. How could they have led him right to it? It was exactly where he said it was in his dream. But when Irratino told him that, Major Red just laughed. "Sure it was." "No, it was." "Irratino, this is a very amusing joke, but I don't understand it. You know the skull is fake. I made it up. So how could it possibly be right here, where I dreamt it was? Obviously you brought it here from wherever you actually found it."

Logico began to explain, but then shook his head. "It's not worth it, Irratino. Let's let him have this one. A six-skull exhibit is almost as good as a seven-skull one." "Okay, Logico." And the two of them walked away. "Do you think he bought it?" Logico asked. "I don't think he noticed the switch at all," Irratino replied, pulling the Ruby Skull of Dennivet from underneath his jacket. "Hopefully, the fake works as well as the real one." And he stared down at it with a kind of care and charm that, frankly, boggled Logico's mind. Logico's not sure what he figured out here. This one was a little too confusing. In the spirit of communism, give yourself $250.

5.1.text:
"It was Comrade Champagne with a fishing spear on the jungle cruiser. Why? For self-righteous reasons!"

"Of course it was me! And I'd do it again. Anybody who would eat such an expensive entree deserves to die." Logico pointed out that Comrade Champagne had, himself, eaten an expensive entree. "Oh, but you see, I knew how to prepare it well. It is true, I am rich. But I am different. I am smart, and I deserve it."

5.2.text:
"It was Silverton the Legend with a machete in the zeppelin. Why? To research a part." "How is researching a part a crime?"

Silverton asked. "Researching a part is not a crime," Logico replied. "But killing someone to research a part is." Silverton looked smug. "But how could part of researching a part be a crime, if researching a part itself is not a crime?" Deductive Logico was momentarily thrown by that: Silverton had heavily researched logic when he played Logico in a major motion picture, and he had gotten good at befuddling people with it.

5.3.text:
"It was Archeologist Ecru with a hammer by the entrance tunnel. Why? To get inside faster!"

"Look, archeology is a dog-eat-dog world. You think these ancient relics are going to be here forever? No! If you don't get there quick, all the good ones are gone. And then you're left empty-handed. All you can do then is study the ancient cultures and learn things about them!" "What's wrong with that?" Irratino replied. "It's not economically lucrative!" Archeologist Ecru replied.

5.4.text:
"It was Executive Producer Steel with a golden lock by the sand fountain. Why? For money (what else?)!"

"Sure, I killed them. But they were inhibiting our ability to escape!" Executive Producer Steel said. "If I hadn't killed them, it would have cost me a fortune. I have places to be. I have meetings I have to attend! Do you know what will happen if I'm not in those meetings?" "Nothing?" Irratino suggested. "Exactly! Now, come on. Let's work together and get out of here!" Fortunately, they had Deductive Logico with them. He was quickly able to ascertain a path out of this room, though he was surprised by the number of combination locks he had to open.

5.5.text:
"It was the Amazing Aureolin with a first-aid kit by the strange machinery. Why? To protect a secret!"

"Fine!" Aureolin declared. "He stumbled in here when I was getting ready for my act, and he saw how I performed my most expensive illusion! I had to do it to protect the Magician's Code! Wait a second... none of you saw how my trick was done, did you?" Before Deductive Logico could tell her that he had, she lunged at him. Our two detectives took off through the ancient temple until they leapt into a small wooden box to hide. However, they learned that this was not a great hiding place when it began to roll. "Logico," Irratino said. "I don't think this is a box... I think it's a mine cart!"

5.6.text:
"It was Hack Blaxton with a ghost trap under the stone archway. Why? To test out a murder method!"

"And it worked!" Hack Blaxton replied. "So I guess I did a great job, didn't I? Now I can incorporate this in my future projects!" "What?!" Logico said. "Why does everybody think they can murder someone for the experience?"

5.7.text:
"It was Art Critic Windsor with a stuffed totem on an altar. Why? Because they ruined the aesthetic!"

"Everything was beautifully coming together," Art Critic Windsor said, "just as I had been promised, and then—this gentleman totally ruined it! So it was either I accept imperfection in the world... or I do something about it. Surely, you will now arrest me for it, which is fine, because it perfectly completes the aesthetic of being a murderer." Logico said that they didn't really have any means to arrest anybody in the jungle, which seemed to really upset Windsor.

5.8.text:
"It was Midnight III with a television camera on the big stage. And it was the grand opening of an amusement park!"

"What a wonderful success this was!" he declared. "And sure, a few people had to die. But statistics regularly prove that in any large construction endeavor, there are a few casualties." Suddenly, it all made sense. Logico grabbed the ancient text from Irratino and exclaimed, "Exactly as I thought! This isn't an ancient text . .. it's an advertisement!" (See Case 5.2; Cutting Through the Jungle.) That's why there had been so many Hollywood stars in the jungle. The strange mazes were simply a series of lines to get into the park (Case 5.3: At the Mouth of Death). That's why there was a hammer and a high-vis vest! Because this place was just recently under construction.

Then, they stumbled into an escape room, one of the smaller amusements at the park (Case 5.4: The Room You Will Never Escape). Then, they stumbled into a back room and mistook a janitor's closet for a ritual chamber (Case 5.5: Into the Depths). The strange machinery were the gears for the minecart ride, which they would board to escape The Amazing Aureolin, starting the ride (Case 5.6: The Mine Train to Destiny/Death). It was decorated with neon signs and flaming pits: just more theming for the park! Finally, they stumbled into the gift shop (Case 5.7: Death in the Bloodred Reliquary), where they mistook the checkout counter for a sacred altar which, in many ways, it was.

Go back over Logico's notes to see how many of the regular trappings of an amusement park our detectives mistook for the trappings of an ancient temple. "So the murders were fake?" Logico asked. "Oh no," Midnight III said, "and, in fact, we would like to thank you for solving all of them by giving you this, the Skull of Ot! It's not really worth anything to us now that we've lost the two eyes." Logico decided he wasn't going to tell them that he had found the two emeralds. Give yourself $10 for each emerald (they turned out to be fake), and another $250 if you figured out that the temple was actually an amusement park!

6.1.text:
"It was Executive Eggplant with a birth certificate in TekCo Tower. And where's the skull? Who cares? It's a skull!"

"Let me talk to the company lawyer before I make a statement," he exclaimed. And then after whispering to a lawyer for a few seconds he said, "I did it and I'll do it again." You might think this means that they have a bad lawyer. But, in fact, it actually means the opposite. Their lawyers are so good you can confess to murder and still get away.

6.2.text:
"It was Grayscale, CPA, with a golden pen in the rooftop garden. And they put their money in a vault of gold coins!"

"Yes, I killed them. But it was for a good reason: they were wasting money!" Everyone at the company agreed that this was a good reason— everyone except Deductive Logico. "Well, how about this, then?" Grayscale, CPA added. "They were wasting a lot of money."

6.3.text:
"It was Computer Ethicist Lemon with a flowerpot by the locked door. And about heights? Hate them, hate them, hate them!"

"I am a force for ethics; ergo, it would be unethical to arrest me," he announced. Logico disagreed, and so did the TekCo security team. But Logico went to Dr. Frankengreen and told him, "Look. See? It wasn't your monster that killed this man." "Still," Dr. Frankengreen replied, "it is only a matter of time.”

6.4.text:
"It was Frankengreen's Monster with a graduated cylinder on the operating table. And he specialized in revengology!"

"I killed him, yes! Because he was covering up the location of my creator! But don't worry, I will find himl" With that, he burst out of the huge doors and disappeared into the night. Just then, Logico came down from the rooftop and breathlessly warned Irratino, "We should watch out! Dr. Frankengreen thinks his monster might kill somebody ...”

6.5.text:
"It was Frankengreen’s Monster with an 'alien' artifact in a desert pad! And his favorite part of New Aegis was that his hated enemy was here!"

"ARGH!" cried Frankengreen's monster. "I thought he was the awful beast, Dr. Frankengreen, who has pursued me to the ends of the Earth." "You can't keep killing people!" Inspector Irratino said. "Regardless of whether you're a monster!" "I am not a monster!" roared Frankengreen's monster, in a very monstrous way. And then he disappeared into the home. "We've got to follow him!" Logico cried. "He's going to try to kill the doctor!"

6.6.text:
"It was CEO Indigo with a family portrait in the courtyard. And he doesn't have a degree!"

"Bah! I came out here to visit Dr. Frankengreen, and I kept getting pestered by fans and people who want money from me. Like orphans! One of them got a little upset at me, so I did what I had to do." "You murdered an orphan?" "No, what are you talking about? There's no money in murdering orphans. I paid them a million dollars to leave. But another guy saw me do it, so I killed him so he wouldn't tell people I might give them a million dollars if they bother me." "So this doesn't have anything to do with Dr. Frankengreen or his monster? You're just going around doing whatever you want with no regard to the throughline?" "I'm a CEO!" Indigo replied.

6.7.text:
"It was Construction Worker Applecore with an ordinary brick in the long hallway. And as for the Skull of Noc: Does he know it? She stole it!"

"So you've caught me again!" replied Applecore, before ripping off his mustache and revealing ... legendary thief Mrs. Ruby! "Fine! I did it! They caught me casing the joint, so I killed them. Is that a crime?!" "Yes," Irratino replied. "That's, like, the definition of a crime!" But Mrs. Ruby had already fled the scene. Dr. Frankengreen looked over the body of his creation and shook his head. "He's finally dead. After all these years. To be honest, I don't know that I feel anything except relief."

6.8.text:
"It was Frankengreen's Monster with bolt cutters near the electrical device. Why? He was Dr. Frankengreen's son!"

"Aha!" cried Frankengreen's monster. He was not dead, and in fact, seemed to be more alive than ever before. "How did you figure it out?" Logico settled in for his lengthy explanation. "Well, let's look at the clues! We found a birth certificate with the father and son's name both scratched out. (See Case 6.1: Making Security Obsolete the Old-Fashioned Way.) Then, we found the diary, clearly written by an angsty teen, in the exact place where the so-called Frankengreen's monster used to be. (See Case 6.3: There Must Be Something We're Overlooking.) Then, we found a picture frame with one of the people in it scratched out. (See Case 6.6: Home Sweet Crime.) All this paints a clear picture of a dysfunctional family life!"

Inspector Irratino had brought popcorn and was now excitingly eating it. "But how did you know that he wasn't his laboratory creation?" "Because," Deductive Logico said, "it's simple: There's only one way to make a person, and it's not from a lightning bolt in a lab. It's the old-fashioned way. And so, if Dr. Frankengreen made a monster, it's much more likely that he is not some kind of misunderstood genius but is, in fact, just your typical bad dad." "Then what about the lab? The slab? What about the lightning rods?!" "Well, Irratino, this is where I admire your whimsy. You see a slab with straps on it, connected to a high-voltage wire, and you think, 'Surely, this was made to create life' But unclouded by the harsh language of Dr.

Frankengreen, it is clear that, in fact, when you electrocute someone, you typically are trying to end their life, not begin it as an experiment." Frankengreen's monster—er, son—admitted it. "Okay, fine! I did it! My father referred to me as a monster my entire life. He chased me, condemned me, looked at me with horror as 'his foul creation'! Mrs. Ruby helped me fake my death, and now, I have killed my father. So what!" "If he was really trying to kill you, pursuing you to the ends of the Earth, chasing you down, then... well, I don't think you committed any crime at all," said Inspector Irratino. "Thank you, detectives," said Frankengreen Jr. "Now I feel that my life can truly begin.

Please allow me to give you a gift, part of my inheritance: this diamond skull. I can only imagine how it fell into my father's possession. Perhaps it was merely another one of his victims." Deductive Logico accepted the diamond skull and gave his thanks. "Now that I have finally killed my father, I can continue with my research. I have a wonderful idea for a potion that will suppress the evil inside of someone, leaving only the good." "Oh?" CEO Indigo said. "That sounds very interesting. We'd love to fund that." Give yourself $250 if you deduced that Dr. Frankengreen's monster was really Dr. Frankengreen's son!

7.1.text:
"It was Elder Ash with an oven on the porch. And she was an expert at potion brewing (specifically alcohol)." "But how?"

Logico asked, at the same time as Irratino asked, "But why?!" "With magick, and because I'm evil!" Elder Ash declared. They both agreed that murderers would mix truth with lies in order to deceive, but they disagreed on which parts were lies, and which parts were truth. Logico believed she was lying about how, and Irratino believed she was lying about why. But neither could find the Skull of Golioc, so they decided to move on to the next coven.

7.2.text:
"It was Mx. Tangerine with the Skull of Golioc in the outdoor meditation space. And their budget was a reasonable amount!"

"This is outrageous! Intolerable! Insidious!" Mx. Tangerine muttered. But, perhaps notably, they did not deny it. Irratino was not worried about whether they were guilty. He was worried about bigger things. "Logico, if that skull is used to kill just two more people... the world will end." "The world's not going to end," Logico said. "But we should take the skull anyway." But when they tried to confiscate it from Mx. Tangerine, it was gone!

7.3.text:
"It was the Duchess of Vermillion with hyperallergenic oil by the central fire. And she was the second-in-command!"

"Haha, you think you’ve stopped us just because you’ve taken one down?!" the Duchess replied. She laughed with a voice that carried through the woods, and brought chills down their spines. "When one witch is taken down, a thousand more rise up in their place! Each one more terrible and more powerful than the last! There's nothing you can do to stop the horror! Together, we will end the world!" Logico had to admit that he was a little nervous about these claims. And Irratino had to admit that it did sound a little evil.

7.4.text:
"It was Archeologist Ecru with a red herring by the bookcases. And her favorite book was How I Murdered My Husband!"

"They objected to us hosting a book club here, so I—with the support of all my witch friends—decided to just get rid of them! And so I did! With the power of my mind! And also a dead fish!" The rest of the witches applauded her actions. Logico and Irratino used the moment to sneak out. Whether they were really magic or really evil was irrelevant: when you're in a group of people and they begin to applaud a murderer, you gotta get out.

7.5.text:
"It was Bishop Azure with the Skull of Golioc in the chapel. And their religious beliefs were that they'd say whatever they need to!"

"Logico!" Irratino interrupted. "Do you see what this means?! If this skull kills one more person, it'll end the world!" "No," Logico said, "if this skull kills one more person, and the legend is true, then it will end the world. And that's a different matter." "Well, surely there's a more-than-zero chance that the lesson is real, isn't there?" "More than zero?" Logico thought. "Maybe." "A maybe-more-than-zero chance is a more-than-zero chance, and if there's a non-zero chance that the world is going to end, we have to take it seriously." "There's a non-zero chance that I'm suddenly going to turn into a block of cheese right this moment! We don't have to take that seriously."

Irratino waited for a moment, and then said, "Well, now we don't. But that was close." Logico groaned. But he agreed to let Irratino keep the skull safe.

7.6.text:
"It was A-List Abalone with a magick wand in the cafeteria. And she loves and supports witches!"

"Why would you kill a witch if you loved and supported them?" Irratino asked. "Isn't it obvious?" Abalone replied. "I did it to bring you two here so I'd have time to steal the amethyst Skull of Golioc from you!" "But you didn't steal it," Irratino said. "I have it locked up here in my briefcase ... wait, no, I've lost it. Logico!" But before either of them could act, Abalone had leapt out the window of the old folks home and fled into the woods. Logico and Irratino followed her.

7.7.text:
"It was A-List Abalone with a shattered snow globe in the moving cave. And their favorite magick word was 'bloon’!"

"Thank goodness!" Inspector Irratino declared. "Oh my gosh, I'm so relieved." "Somebody was murdered, Irratino!" Logico replied. "Yes, but not with the Skull of Golioc! Ha-ha! The world survives for another day! But wait! What is Tourist Tulip going to do with it?"

7.8.text:
"It was Hedge Witch Skobeloff with the Skull of Golioc near the pit. Why? To scare people away!"

Logico stood up to give his famous speech. "By studying the spellbook, I learned something: This spellbook is fake. It's way scarier than it should be. Why would this be the spellbook that a group of witches would use? It has six spells on how to murder people and none on how to get to work more quickly. It's completely impractical. There is only one type of reader it could be intended for: a rube who is being tricked into fearing the witches. "I first realized it when I saw that several of the witches were idolizing Major Red. I saw a poster in the dark woods that read, A TERRIFIED ENEMY IS EASY TO BEAT.

(See Case 7.5: Stop This Nunsense.) "Additionally, I noticed one of the items that was for sale at the crystal shop in New Aegis—a vial of red liquid—was exactly the same shade as the blood!" (See Case 7.2: It's Crystal Clear It's Murder!) "Clearly, a sign that the first murder was faked! "Putting this all together, and knowing that you did not murder someone with a magick spell—and, like Irratino knew, that you were not mean enough to do it, either—led me to one inevitable conclusion: that you were pretending to be bad so that people would leave you alone." Hedge Witch Skobeloff scoffed. "Fine! You got it! People love to bother witches. In the worst-case scenario, of course, they try to get us burned at the stake.

But even in the best-case scenario, it's just annoying questions or requests for love spells. We want to have time to read! So we did what we had to: We made up the worst and most horrible rumors about witches and then we spread them to anyone who would listen, and it worked!" "Well," Irratino said, "it worked until we heard about it." "In a way, then," Logico said, "it actually had the opposite effect." "Well, you two, this might surprise you to hear, but a lot of people are more afraid than they are curious." "A sad state of affairs," Irratino said. "But fortunately, you only need one person who's curious to balance out all the rest being too afraid."

"We'll let you off with a warning this time," Logico said, "but please don't do it again. You've wasted a lot of our time that could have been useful for investigating real murders. And now we're very much behind." "And, if you don't mind,"Inspector Irratino said, "we’ll be taking this for our trouble." And with that, they grabbed the Amethyst Skull of Golioc and were on their way. Give yourself $250 if you deduced that the witches were only pretending to be evil in order to scare people away! (And give yourself an extra $100 if you deduced that the Demon King was actually Mrs. Ruby in disguise!)

8.1.text:
"It was Mayor Honey with the Skull of Eseth by a big pumpkin pie!"

"Fine! I did it! But to be honest, I don't regret it at all!" Mayor Honey exclaimed. "The people in town are going to expect me to be able to cut taxes and increase spending, and I don't want to let them down. It'll be much better to serve the rest of my term behind bars. Then I have an excuse for why I wasn't able to do what I said."

8.2.text:
"It was Ex-Husband Earthtone with a typewriter by Dame Obsidian's actual bookcase!"

"That inglorious fellow right there had the temerity to insult my ex-wife! I couldn't stand for that, of course, so I picked up the typewriter and hit him over the head. That’ll teach him to insult my ex-wife." "But how could it teach him anything if it killed him?" Logico asked. "Well, he's not going to do it again, is he?"

8.3.text:
"It was Docent Windsor with A History of Sea Legends near a giant map wall!"

"Sure, I did it! But can you blame me? He kept touching the exhibits! I said, 'Please don't touch the exhibits.' And yet he kept touching them! I said, 'Move away from the exhibits!' And yet he stayed near. So instead of asking him, I showed him! And I don't think he'll be touching any more exhibits anytime soon." Curator Coppertone did not fully approve of this method. But then again, he wasn't totally against it, either. I mean, after all, now nobody was touching the exhibits, were they?

8.4.text:
"It was Lady Violet with the Big Red Book in front of the portrait of Major Red!"

"I couldn't believe the horrid lies that Major Red had written in this book ... at first. But the more I read about it, the more I thought that maybe he was on to something. And so, inspired by his writing, I struck down this rich art collector." "Really?" Logico said. "You were persuaded by the power of his writing? You've turned your back on your class and joined Major Red's revolution?" "Haha, no, I'm joking. I killed this guy because he outbid me for a painting last week."

8.5.text:
"It was Temple Guard Teal with the Skull of Ot in the vine corner. And he fondly recalled getting paid!"

"He kept calling me Temple Guard Teal! But that's not my name! That's just a character I played when I was working at the opening of an amusement park! My real name is Marengo, and I'm an actor in Hollywood! And if you believed my temple performance—or were awed by the conviction of my murder—then I would love it if you would cast me in your projects." Deductive Logico had to remind Temple Guard Teal that this was real life, not an audition, and that he was much more likely to end up in jail than he was in the movies.

8.6.text:
"It was Vice President Mauve with a bust of CEO Indigo near the electrical panel. And she knows a Mac from a PC!"

"You'll be hearing from my lawyers, my employees, and my investors!" she said. "This company is going to sue this museum for so much that you won't even have a building to live in." "Why would you sue the museum?" Logico asked. "Because if we're known for being wildly litigious, then people will think twice about turning us in for murder."

8.7.text:
"It was Black Cat Midnight Baby with a gingerbread house in front of a huge window. And her favorite magick word was 'meow’!"

"You scoundrel!" replied Inspector Irratino. "How dare you accuse such a cutie?!" "Meow!" said Black Cat Midnight Baby. "What?! What do you mean you confess?! How could you even kill them?!" "MEOW!" replied Black Cat Midnight Baby. Irratino just shook his head. "I can't believe this cat. Lock her up and throw away the key."

8.8.text:
"It was Curator Coppertone with a flier advertising the exhibit in a luxury bathroom. Why? To steal the Seven Skulls!"

"What are you talking about?!" cried the curator. "I wouldn't need to steal the skulls. I own the skulls! They're my skulls!" "That's what you wanted us to think!" Logico said. "But this explains several of the strange things we've encountered. To recap, when I first arrived, you said somebody had stolen all the skulls." "Mrs. Ruby stole them, you proved it!" Curator Coppertone replied. "Well, let's review the crime: your assistant was murdered, the security system was engaged, and the doors were all locked. Somehow, someone had snuck the skulls out and planted them all over the world... a seemingly impossible crime. We all believed that Mrs. Ruby had done it, but how could she?" "You'll never know," Mrs. Ruby replied.

"We'll never know because you didn't do it. Mrs. Ruby was blamed for the crime, and she accepted the blame because it bolstered her reputation as a thief, but she didn't do it." "Then who did steal the skulls?!" asked Inspector Irratino, who always loved hearing Logico's wrap-ups. "Nobody stole them!" Logico said. "Because they were never here to begin with! In fact, Curator Coppertone tricked us into going out and stealing them all for him. That's why several of the skulls seemed to have been where they were for longer than they'd been stolen. And that's why the fliers advertising the Seven Skulls Exhibit were all recent (see Case 8: The Remarkable Rooftop Reveal)." "But why would Curator Coppertone do such a thing?!"

Irratino asked, not really because he didn't know—he had his suspicions—but because he delighted in playing the role of the surprised listener during a Big Reveal monologue. "He has years of respected experience!" "Because this isn't Curator Coppertone!" Logico declared. "No, in fact, this is Curator Coppertone's assistant!" "But we saw Curator Coppertone's assistant! He's dead!" "That was the real Curator Coppertone! That's why there was a giant framed painting of him on the wall: Who frames a giant painting of one's assistant?" "It's not true!" cried Curator Coppertone. "You can't prove it." "Ah, perhaps that would be true," Logico said. "Except you couldn't resist one last taunt.

The names of the skulls themselves: "The Topaz Skull of Eseth. "The Obsidian Skull of Nasem. "The Sapphire Skull of Rewe. "The Ruby Skull of Dennivet. "The Emerald Skull of Ot. "The Diamond Skull of Noc "And last, but not least, the Amethyst Skull of Golioc." "What about them?" the so-called Coppertone asked. "Each of the names is an anagram. And when you unscramble the words, what do they spell?" Irratino grabbed a pencil and worked it out: "THESE NAMES WERE INVENTED TO CON LOGICO." "And that is why there was a supernatural mystery surrounding each skull! Because the skulls were chosen because of their publicity value! To draw people to this museum and to create a sensation!" Curator Coppertone stood up and declared, "Fine, Logico!

You're right! I was Curator Coppertone's assistant, but Curator Coppertone was running this place into the ground! So I killed him and took his place. Then, I killed two bodies with one stone: I created a fake crime, and I framed Mrs. Ruby for it! But you'll rue the day you accused me of this crime even if I did commit it!" "Oh, yeah?" Logico said. "Why is that?" "Because I'm definitely not going to pay you for solving these cases now!" But Irratino, who could not care less about money, said, "Don't worry, Logico! I still appreciate you clearing my name. And such marvelous deduction work, too." "Yes, Logico, what a wonderful job," Mrs. Ruby said. "Unfortunately, you've done the opposite of clearing my name.

People thought I’d pulled off an impossible heist, and now, I have a reputation to uphold!" And with that, she took off with the Seven Skulls. "She's getting away with the relics we rightfully stole!" Irratino shouted. He took off after Mrs. Ruby, leaving Logico behind to deal with Curator Coppertone and the Museum of Mysticality and, as always, the paperwork. But Logico didn't mind. He loved doing paperwork, and he was looking forward to adding up how much he would have been paid, if he hadn't accused the person who had hired him. Then, he would write down everything he could remember about these adventures and send his notes to Chalk Publications to be turned into puzzles and published.

They had already thought of a great name for this collection: The Case of the Seven Skulls. Hopefully, everyone else would enjoy solving them just as much as Logico!
